column12: a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug, and that is what makes it consistent with discontinuation_pct. The two are the same measurement: at the Part B allowed rate of $30.713 a mg, a full labelled year of 6,240 mg is $191,647, and $71,752 / $191,647 = 0.3744, which is exactly the share of a labelled year the discontinuation row derives from dosage units per beneficiary. Pairing the $207,087 labelled-year WAC with the same 0.6256 would count the shortfall twice, once in the price and once in the stopping rate. The ratio between the two figures is itself informative: a nivolumab patient consumes about 35% of a labelled year

column12: measured on the same beneficiaries the price above is quoted on, which is the point: under a constant hazard in a steady state the share of a year's treated patients still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, so the engine's stock is the count of beneficiaries that price applies to. Measured across every labelled indication rather than taken from one trial's median, which is right for an asset-level rate on a product sold in a dozen tumours.
